items.title: Telangana Assembly passes CURE Bill replacing 1955 GHMC Act
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Telangana Core Urban Region (Integrated Governance) Bill, 2026 (CURE Bill) was passed by the Assembly on September 12, Saturday. The Bill replaces the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) Act, 1955, and establishes a unified governance framework for Hyderabad’s Core Urban Region (CURE), which currently includes three municipal corporations — the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, Cyberabad Municipal Corporation, and Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation. A draft of the CURE Bill was released for public consultation earlier on July 5. The Bill was passed with an amendment that reduces the maximum proposed annual increase in property tax to 10% from the 20% hike proposed in the draft. One of the biggest changes under the CURE Bill is the proposed shift in how property tax is assessed. The existing Annual Rental Value (ARV) system will be replaced by a Capital Value System (CVS), under which property tax will be linked to the government's market value of the property — the value used for registration purposes. items.title: Nearly 25% in Srikakulam’s Uddanam screened so far have kidney disease: Study
items.summary: Nearly one in four people screened so far in Andhra Pradesh’s Uddanam region have been found to have kidney disease, according to an interim analysis of an ongoing study aimed at identifying the causes of the region’s long-running kidney disease crisis. Of the 3,897 people screened so far, 949, or 24.35%, were found to have kidney disease, The Hindu reported. Of these, 550 were diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD), while 399 were found to have chronic kidney disease of unknown aetiology (CKDu), according to an official statement issued on Saturday, September 12. The findings were presented to state Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav by the team of experts conducting the study. Uddanam, a cluster of villages in the Srikakulam district of north coastal Andhra Pradesh, has for decades reported unusually high levels of kidney disease and deaths linked to renal failure. The problem has been documented since the early 1990s and has previously prompted studies by several institutions, including the Indian Council of Medical Research and Andhra University Medical College. items.title: Telangana SIR: Activists flag vague notices, seek transparency in hearings
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A group of activists in Telangana monitoring the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise have flagged several concerns with the notice phase. The draft electoral roll for Telangana was published on August 17, and the period for issuing notices began immediately and will continue until November 5. The final electoral roll will be published on November 11. In a representation to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Telangana Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) C Sudharshan Reddy, the activists said there was a lack of transparency in the SIR notices and hearings. They said there was no mechanism to check the current status of those who had been issued notices, and that notices were being issued without the application of mind in cases involving ‘logical discrepancies’. People across Telangana have started receiving notices for different reasons, such as non-mapping with the 2002 SIR, name mismatch, father’s or mother’s name mismatch, or unusual age differences flagged as logical discrepancies. items.title: Why Kerala is facing power cuts, and why the crisis has become a political fight
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Kerala's power crisis has now moved beyond an inconvenience for households and businesses to a political fight over a more fundamental question: why does the state repeatedly find itself short of electricity when demand rises or hydel generation falls? Partial power cuts have continued for nearly two weeks, with outages being imposed during evening peak hours and reports from several parts of the state of multiple cuts extending into the night. The disruption has hit students, families with young children, and people working from home, while the lack of advance information about some outages has added to public anger. The government has now said it will put in place a system to alert consumers about planned restrictions at the feeder level. The crisis has also exposed Kerala’s dependence on electricity purchased from outside the state. Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph has said Kerala can generate only around 25% of the electricity it consumes, with the rest coming from the central grid and power purchase agreements with generators outside the state.
